primary_claim: Cheese-seeking behavior in a maze-solving RL policy is spatially localized around the cheese's position, even though the presence of cheese is linearly decodable at near-perfect accuracy from activations at nearly every layer of the network; sensitivity of activations to cheese proximity is concentrated in later layers, especially the fully-connected layer preceding the value head.

models.family: procgen maze CNN policy (Langosco et al. goal-misgeneralization agent)

effect.metric: linear probe accuracy for cheese-presence detection across network layers
effect.value: near-perfect accuracy in most layers, dropping to 90% at the policy head

contradicts_or_qualifies: Authors' initial hypothesis (informed by Shard Theory and Turner et al.'s maze-policy work) was that cheese representation, not just behavioral influence, would be spatially localized to later layers; instead cheese presence was found encoded with high accuracy across nearly all layers, contradicting this initial hypothesis even though behavioral influence itself remained localized
stated_future_work: Analysis of probing failure cases in later layers to uncover common patterns where the cheese-shard is not activated or not linearly detectable
Identification and patching of a hypothesized cheese-mouse distance feature in layer embedder.block3.res1.resadd_out to observe resulting behavioral changes
Generalization to other environmental influences (e.g. maze-traversal behavior) to establish general principles of shard mechanics
Cross-architecture comparisons to test whether shard-like structures are architecture-dependent or a general property of RL systems
limitations_stated: Limited generalizability: study focuses on a single policy trained in a specific environment
Limited to a single neural network architecture
All experiments involve scenarios far outside the agent's training distribution
Study confined to fixed 15x15 mazes, without exploring other maze sizes
Findings show correlation between cheese presence, agent behavior and layer activation but do not establish causality
quote: Our findings suggest that while all network layers consistently encode the presence of cheese, the effect of this information on the agent's behavior is spatially localized within the maze environment.
